subject: APAC edge maintenance: minimizing KV-cache impact and staggered restarts
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finserv.io>, ops@finserv.io
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 00:12:00 +0800
Subject: APAC edge maintenance: minimizing KV-cache impact and staggered restarts

Hello Samantha / FinServ ops team,

We have a scheduled maintenance window for a subset of our APAC edge nodes to apply a NIC driver and kernel micro-update. This is a rolling process designed to preserve request continuity, but we expect brief disruptions for sessions that rely on long-lived KV caches.

Window (proposed):
- Start: 2026-11-12 01:00 (UTC+8)
- End: 2026-11-12 03:00 (UTC+8)
- Regions: APAC-edge pools (apac1, apac2, apac-east) — nodes will be staggered to avoid simultaneous evictions.

What to expect:
- Brief p99 latency spikes lasting 15-45s for affected requests while a node drains and restarts; in-flight streaming may reconnect.
- KV-cache entries tied to node-local caches may become unavailable during the short eviction; we will automatically warm caches for new requests where feasible.
- No customer data will be moved outside your configured region.

Mitigations we will run during the window:
- Canary on 2% of traffic 2 hours before the main window (we will notify you separately if you want to opt out).
- Prefix-preservation attempt: where you pin model sessions, we will try to steer subsequent requests to warm nodes.
- Automatic fallback to a compatible model variant with cold-start-friendly settings if a node remains unavailable longer than 5 minutes.

Attachments: maintenance_readme.pdf (runbook) and apac_staggered_plan.csv (per-node schedule).

Action items for FinServ: please reply by EOD Mon 2026-11-09 if you have blackout constraints or if you run long-lived streaming sessions that cannot tolerate reconnections — we will carve out those tenants from the initial roll or schedule a separate low-impact window.

Thanks,

— Lauren Bishop

Thanks Lauren — a couple of technical notes for the customer email that I want to call out so expectations are precise:

On Thu, 5 Nov 2026 at 00:12 +0800, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> We have a scheduled maintenance window for a subset of our APAC edge nodes to apply a NIC driver and kernel micro-update.

- The p99 spike estimate (15–45s) is conservative for most request patterns; for long-lived streaming (server-sent events / websockets) we may see a 60–90s reconnection event in the worst-case while the upstream LB finishes requeueing.
- KV-cache: we use a two-tier approach (local hot cache + global prefix cache). Local-only entries are most at risk; global prefix keys will survive. Recommend customers use prefix-based cache keys where possible before the window.
- We will run the canary at 23:00 on 11/11 (UTC+8) using a subset of apac-east. If the canary fails, we will delay the main window by 24 hours and notify all stakeholders.

I've updated the runbook with an explicit rollback checklist and added the staging job id. Please attach the runbook link to the customer message.

-- Monica
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha — quick responses inline and next steps.

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 08:35 AM +0800, Samantha Lee wrote:
> - If a session reconnects, will session affinity and any streaming offsets be preserved automatically?

- Short answer: offsets are preserved when the client resumes from the last-acked token if the client uses the standard resume API/ACK pattern. For naïve reconnects, your downstream should handle duplicate/overlap at the application layer; we recommend the SDK resume flow for live streams.

> - For the canary, which node pool will take the canary traffic?

- Canary pool: apac-east (small set of nodes in the apac-east edge pool). We'll coordinate a 30-minute window on 2026-11-11 23:00–23:30 (UTC+8). If you want to join the canary, we can whitelist your staging tenancy — reply with the staging tenancy id and we will add it.

> - Any specific SDK/client versions we should avoid during the window?

- Avoid client versions older than 2.7.1 for streaming (there was a reconnect race fixed in 2.7.1). We'll include a note in the runbook.

Next steps:
- If FinServ wants to join the canary, reply with the staging tenancy id by EOD 2026-11-09.
- We'll run the canary at 23:00 on 11/11 and publish the canary report by 02:00 on 11/12.
- If there are any blackout constraints, let us know by EOD 2026-11-09 and we'll exclude those tenancies from the initial roll.

Attaching updated runbook and per-node schedule. I'll set up a short 20-min sync if you'd like a live walkthrough.

Best,
